teaser.text: Most people meet Midea Group through an appliance, but the company also sells the machinery, systems and services behind homes, buildings and factories. To understand its business, follow the money from the customer’s need to Midea’s products, then through the costs and working capital that determine what remains.

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is HK$86.42 in October 2027, a 3% loss including dividends, and HK$98.90 in October 2029, a 24% gain including dividends. The bear, base and bull cases carry 27%, 53% and 20% probabilities.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Midea Group, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: At HK$94.55, Midea can reach a weighted HK$98.90 by October 2029, but that outcome hinges on resilient appliance earnings, overseas expansion and better industrial returns. Management expects mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth in 2026 with a stable net margin. It also expects overseas own-brand sales to accelerate and ToB sales to outgrow ToC sales; ToB means sales to businesses and ToC means sales to individual consumers.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Midea Group really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is what remains after operating cash pays for investment and financing-related outflows. Capital spending reached RMB11,141.889 million in 2025, and free cash flow fell 22.2%. Deducting stock compensation produces “real” free cash flow, because issuing shares to employees costs existing owners even when it does not immediately use cash.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Midea Group today?

paragraphs.text: At HK$94.55, a trailing P/E of 13.8 means investors pay HK$13.80 for each HK$1 of recent annual profit. The forward P/E of 12.1 uses an estimate for the next twelve months, so it assumes earnings will rise. At the same price, the two multiples imply earnings per share of about HK$6.85 and HK$7.81, or roughly 14% growth. The stock therefore depends on forecast profit arriving.

dividend.opening: Midea Group's dividend rose from CNY1.70 to CNY4.30 over the historical five-year increase, with base dividends forecast at CNY4.80 in October 2027 and CNY5.80 in October 2029. Midea Group's dividends and buybacks totalled RMB42,185.673 million in 2025, or 109.4% of free cash flow, so the dividend was funded partly from accumulated resources rather than that year's free cash flow alone.
dividend.closing: The full Midea Group memo also covers its business, rivals, management decisions and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Midea Group pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Base dividends are CNY4.80 in October 2027 and CNY5.30 in October 2028. They reach CNY5.80 in October 2029. This is measured growth below the historical five-year increase from CNY1.70 to CNY4.30, while the proposed CNY0.50 interim dividend supports the first forecast window.

blocks.heading: Does Midea Group's dividend fit its cash flow?

paragraphs.text: That decline coincided with an unusually large distribution. Dividends and buybacks totalled RMB42,185.673 million in 2025, or 109.4% of free cash flow. The company could do this because one year’s free cash flow is not the same as all available cash: a business can use savings, sell investments or change its borrowing.

The broader cash position remained strong. Investment sales and maturities exceeded investment purchases, while debt repayments exceeded new borrowing. Net cash reached RMB173,632.913 million at year-end, compared with RMB66,024.231 million in 2021. This supports the affordability of the period’s distributions, but it does not prove that every acquisition earned a satisfactory return.

blocks.heading: What could change Midea Group's dividend?

paragraphs.text: The bear dividend stays at CNY4.30, while the bull reaches CNY5.20, CNY6.20 and CNY7.20. The bear reflects shareholder payouts already exceeding free cash flow, while the bull requires stronger cash generation.
The first signal would be replacement demand after subsidy pull-forward. Weak sell-through in 2027–2028 would lower revenue, increase discounting and push the forecast toward the bear case.

earnings.title: Midea Group earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Midea Group next results are expected on October 29, 2026; guidance is mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth with a stable net margin.
earnings.opening: Midea Group's next results are expected on October 29, 2026. Midea Group must show whether sales accelerated enough to support the latest full-year growth range.
earnings.closing: The full Midea Group memo also answers how Midea Group makes money, who its rivals are, how management is aligned, and what risks it faces.

blocks.heading: What has Midea Group guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: Management guidance is the company’s own forecast; an analyst estimate is an outsider’s calculation. For 2026, the latest analyst account describes mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth and a stable net margin. Revenue is money earned from sales, while net margin is the share left as profit after expenses and tax.

Management also expects ToB sales to outgrow ToC sales. ToB means selling to businesses; ToC means selling to consumers. Selling air-conditioners to a property developer is ToB, while selling one through a shop to a household is ToC. Larger business orders may be more predictable, but both channels require factories, distribution, marketing and after-sales service. More sales will count as progress only if they preserve profit. That is the standard analysts will apply to their forecasts.

blocks.heading: Has Midea Group kept its promises to shareholders?

paragraphs.text: Midea paid the interim dividend, approved the final dividend and changed a buyback plan from employee incentives to cancellation. Alignment is strongest when rewards clear demanding hurdles, cash reaches owners and cancellation actually reduces the share count. That brings us to how minority owners are treated in the company’s two share lines and connected dealings.

blocks.heading: What is Midea Group's revenue and profit trend?

paragraphs.text: Revenue was RMB261,052.379 million, up 3.5% in the first half of 2026. Operating income fell 1.9% to RMB31,743.624 million. Gross margin declined from 25.5% to 25.0%, while operating margin reached 12.2%. Midea attributed pressure to weaker domestic appliance demand, lower selling prices, higher raw-material costs, trade-policy effects and renminbi appreciation. Selling more can therefore produce less operating profit per unit.
